summary.headline: Inox Wind Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue flat YoY at INR1,306 crore; FY27 guidance of ~75% revenue growth and 20%+ EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA of INR333 crore, PBT of INR216 crore, PAT of INR106 crore and cash profit of INR268 crore, with FY26 revenue of about INR4,500 crore against an earlier INR5,000 crore target. Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

financial_highlights.value: INR4,600 crore against INR5,000 crore guideline
financial_highlights.change: INR400 crore shortfall expected to be recovered in Q1-Q2 FY27
about INR40 crore from acquisition-linked debt, about INR10 crore value-added services, about INR10 crore treasury

segments.name: Inox Wind (WTG/EPC)
segments.commentary: Consolidated Q4 revenue INR1,306 crore flat YoY with EBITDA INR333 crore; order book 3.1 GW, with about 600 MW added in FY26, and visibility of more than 24 months. Only about 500 MW of the order book is from group company Inox Clean.

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M / evacuation)
segments.commentary: Portfolio 13+ GWp (about 10.5 GW wind, rest solar) with 96.5% average machine availability; Q4 EBITDA INR57 crore on about INR120 crore total income. Management says O&M margins are about 50%, and FY27 EBITDA is guided at above INR600 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 (approx. INR7,500 crore on a INR4,500 crore base), with EBITDA margin of about 20% (stated as '20% to 20%').

Inox Green FY27 EBITDA guidance of upwards of INR600 crore, with management saying consolidation of two acquisitions (about 6.5 GW of wind O&M assets) will lift FY27 consol EBITDA and PAT multifold over FY26.
Group Inox Clean targets about 14 GW capacity by FY29, adding about 3 GW+ annually, of which 20-30% is expected to be wind, to drive recurring orders for Inox Wind.
New 4.4 MW turbine on track for approvals and commercial launch within calendar 2026, expected to aid penetration and margins.
Most EPC projects expected to be completed by H1 FY27, except one leading job, after which projects await statutory compliances for commissioning.
capex_capacity: Inox Green's two acquisitions cover about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets; entity one order expected within a couple of weeks, entity two expected within 60-90 days.

Evacuation infrastructure demerger from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions approved by NCLT Ahmedabad; about INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50-55 crore annual depreciation removed. Completion expected in 1-2 months.
Cranes moving in-house (half in-house, a couple more due this year); power transformer manufacturing started last year and ramping up.
Management plans to expand into power electronics (transformers, inverters, power electronics, ECS) with details to follow in coming months.
Group Inox Clean has about 2 GW installed, 6 GW solar module and 3 GW cell capacity; targets 10 GW each of IPP, cell and module over about 15 months.
demand_pricing: Order book 3.1 GW, diversified; recent wins include Aditya Birla, Gentari/Amplus, Jakson Green, First Energy and Leap Green. Multiple customer negotiations near closure.
Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to move to 75% equipment supply (management also cited 75-80%).

Management says margins are guided at about 20% or higher on equipment supply; equipment supply is on LC terms, passing steel price changes through, reducing exposure to land/ROW cost and payment delays.
Revenue mix: about 10% O&M and 90% Inox Wind currently; O&M expected to rise to about 18-20% of consolidated revenue.
Management said it does not have FY27 order inflow targets and is 'sold out' for about 2.5 years on its stated ambitions.

qa_highlights.question: How will the two Inox Green acquisitions contribute to EBITDA and when will they be consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions carry roughly 50% EBITDA margins, as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems. Entity one's order is expected within a couple of weeks; entity two is 60-90 days away, and all revenues from 1 April 2026 are to be reflected in consolidated results.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 working capital position against the INR5,000 crore guideline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it achieved INR4,600 crore against the INR5,000 crore guideline, with the INR400 crore balance expected in Q1-Q2 FY27 after supply-chain issues from delayed imported ECS components.

qa_highlights.question: What was actual MW execution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give megawatt execution, saying the company guides on revenue only, and reiterated this stated policy.

qa_highlights.question: Will equipment supply shift raise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins stay at about 20% or higher, with equipment supply carrying less risk and more upfront cash; O&M at about 50% margin would add a higher-margin bias.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall QoQ from about INR78 crore to INR69 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarterly variation to value-added services timing (about INR8-9 crore) and said the annualised run-rate is the right measure.

risks_watch: Working capital: about INR400 crore of FY26 working capital target still outstanding, expected in Q1-Q2 FY27; PSU customer payment delays noted.
Execution: reliance on imported ECS components, shipping delays and commodity cost increases; geopolitical risk cited as cause of revenue miss.
Credibility: FY26 revenue of INR4,500 crore was below the INR5,000 crore target and Q4 revenue was flat YoY; management declined to disclose MW execution.
Acquisition and demerger timing: two acquisitions and IRSL demerger completion dates remain uncertain; consolidation of about 6.5 GW O&M assets underpins the INR600 crore FY27 EBITDA guidance.
Inox Green's other income of about INR40 crore a quarter from acquisition-related debt is non-operating; management acknowledged core EBITDA margin excluding it is about 45%.
Capital allocation and dividend policy for Inox Green not yet defined; management said a policy would follow consolidation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on strategy, group synergies and the FY27 guidance, but defensive on the FY26 shortfall, attributing it to geopolitical events. Management was evasive on MW execution and on the Inox Renewable Solutions earnings profile, and deferred dividend and capital allocation questions.

we have now pivoted the company on a much stronger footing
we expect our consolidated revenue to grow by around 75% over FY26 with EBITDA margin to be 20% to 20%.
As we have communicated on the last call, we are not giving any megawatt -specific guidances.
